title: 0.96" OLED
description: Show “Hello!” and a counter on a 0.96-inch SSD1306 OLED display.
idea: The 0.96 inch SSD1306 OLED shows "Hello!" and a counter that goes up every second
goal: Show “Hello!” and a counter on a 0.96-inch SSD1306 OLED display.
behavior: The display shows “Hello!” and the counter, starting at 0.
The counter increases by one every second.

parts.purpose: show “Hello!” and the counter.

code:
from machine import Pin, I2C
from ssd1306 import SSD1306_I2C
import time

# Set up the OLED screen using the wired I2C pins.
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(16), scl=Pin(17), freq=400000)
oled = SSD1306_I2C(128, 64, i2c)

# Start the counter at zero.
counter = 0

# Show the greeting and current counter once each second.
while True:
    oled.fill(0)
    oled.title("Hello!")
    oled.center_text("Hello!", 20)
    oled.center_text("Count: " + str(counter), 40)
    oled.show()
    time.sleep(1)
    counter += 1
explanation: The program shows “Hello!” and a counter on the OLED, starting at 0. It updates the display and increases the counter once every second.

title: Active buzzer
description: Make an active buzzer beep twice every three seconds.
idea: The active buzzer module beeps twice every 3 seconds
goal: Make an active buzzer beep twice every three seconds.
behavior: The buzzer beeps twice, with a short pause between beeps.
It waits until the next three-second cycle and repeats.

parts.purpose: beep twice each cycle

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set the beep and pause times in seconds.
BEEP_TIME = 0.2
SHORT_PAUSE = 0.2
CYCLE_WAIT = 2.4

# Set up the buzzer so it starts quiet.
buzzer = Pin(16, Pin.OUT, value=1)

# Beep twice, then wait for the next three-second cycle.
while True:
    buzzer.value(0)
    time.sleep(BEEP_TIME)
    buzzer.value(1)
    time.sleep(SHORT_PAUSE)
    buzzer.value(0)
    time.sleep(BEEP_TIME)
    buzzer.value(1)
    time.sleep(CYCLE_WAIT)
explanation: The buzzer beeps twice, with a short pause between beeps. It stays quiet for the rest of the three-second cycle, and the pin is HIGH whenever the buzzer is quiet.

title: BH1750 light sensor
description: Use the Pico’s built-in LED to show when the BH1750 measures less than 20 lux.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the BH1750 measures less than 20 lux, for example when you cover it with your hand.
goal: Use the Pico’s built-in LED to show when the BH1750 measures less than 20 lux.
behavior: The Pico’s built-in LED turns on when the BH1750 measures less than 20 lux.
The LED turns off when the light level is 20 lux or higher.

parts.purpose: measure light level in lux, including when covered by a hand.

code:
from machine import Pin, I2C
import time

# Set the light level that turns the LED on.
LOW_LIGHT_LIMIT = 20

# Set up the I2C connection and the built-in LED.
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(16), scl=Pin(17), freq=400000)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Find the sensor address and start continuous high-resolution readings.
if 0x23 in i2c.scan():
    sensor_address = 0x23
else:
    sensor_address = 0x5C
i2c.writeto(sensor_address, b"\x10")
time.sleep_ms(180)

# Read the light level and update the LED repeatedly.
while True:
    data = i2c.readfrom(sensor_address, 2)
    lux = (data[0] << 8 | data[1]) / 1.2
    if lux < LOW_LIGHT_LIMIT:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(0.12)
explanation: The program reads the BH1750 light sensor over I2C and converts its reading to lux. The built-in LED turns on below 20 lux and turns off at 20 lux or higher.

title: BME280
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the BME280 temperature rises 2 °C above its starting temperature.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the BME280's temperature is 2 °C higher than when the program started, for example when you hold it between your fingers
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the BME280 temperature rises 2 °C above its starting temperature.
behavior: At startup, the program records the BME280 temperature.
The Pico’s built-in LED turns on when the temperature is at least 2 °C above that starting temperature.
The LED turns off if the temperature falls below the threshold.

parts.purpose: measure temperature changes in the air near the sensor, including warming from your fingers.

code:
from machine import Pin, I2C
from bme280 import BME280
import time

# Set the temperature rise needed to turn on the LED.
RISE_LIMIT = 2.0

# Set up the BME280 sensor and the Pico's built-in LED.
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(16), scl=Pin(17), freq=400000)
sensor = BME280(i2c)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Record the starting temperature and begin with the LED off.
t, p, h = sensor.read()
starting_temperature = t
led.off()

# Check the temperature and update the LED about once a second.
while True:
    t, p, h = sensor.read()
    if t >= starting_temperature + RISE_LIMIT:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(1)
explanation: At startup, the program records the BME280 temperature as the starting temperature. It checks the sensor about once a second and turns the built-in LED on when the temperature is at least 2 °C higher, turning it off again when it falls below that point.

title: DHT22
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when humidity rises at least 10 percentage points above the startup reading.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the DHT22's humidity is 10 % higher than when the program started, for example when you breathe on it
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when humidity rises at least 10 percentage points above the startup reading.
behavior: At startup, the Pico records the DHT22 humidity as the baseline.
The Pico checks humidity no more than once every 2 seconds.
The built-in LED turns on when humidity is at least 10 percentage points above the baseline; otherwise, it stays off.

parts.purpose: Measure the air’s humidity near the Pico.

code:
from machine import Pin
import dht
import time

# Set up the sensor and the built-in LED.
sensor = dht.DHT22(Pin(16))
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Wait before the first reading and prepare to save the startup humidity.
time.sleep(1)
baseline = None

# Read humidity at least two seconds apart and control the LED.
while True:
    try:
        sensor.measure()
        humidity = sensor.humidity()

        # Save the first good reading as the baseline.
        if baseline is None:
            baseline = humidity

        # Turn on the LED only when humidity rises by 10 points or more.
        if humidity >= baseline + 10:
            led.value(1)
        else:
            led.value(0)
    except OSError:
        # Ignore a failed reading and try again in the next round.
        pass

    # Leave enough time before measuring again.
    time.sleep(2)
explanation: The program waits one second, then saves the first successful humidity reading as its baseline. It checks again every two seconds and turns on the built-in LED when humidity is at least 10 percentage points above that baseline; failed readings are retried.

title: DS18B20
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the DS18B20 reads at least 2 °C above the temperature at startup.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the DS18B20's temperature is 2 °C higher than when the program started, for example when you hold it between your fingers
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the DS18B20 reads at least 2 °C above the temperature at startup.
behavior: At startup, the program records the DS18B20’s temperature.
The built-in LED turns on when the temperature reaches 2 °C or more above that starting temperature.

parts.purpose: measure temperature changes from startup, such as when held between your fingers.

code:
from machine import Pin
import onewire
import ds18x20
import time

# Set the temperature rise needed to turn on the LED.
RISE_LIMIT = 2.0

# Set up the sensor on GP16 and the built-in LED.
ow = onewire.OneWire(Pin(16))
ds = ds18x20.DS18X20(ow)
roms = ds.scan()
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Keep the LED off if no sensor is found.
if not roms:
    led.value(0)
    while True:
        time.sleep(1)

# Read the starting temperature to use as the reference.
ds.convert_temp()
time.sleep_ms(750)
start_temp = ds.read_temp(roms[0])

# Read the sensor and turn on the LED after a 2 degree rise.
while True:
    ds.convert_temp()
    time.sleep_ms(750)
    current_temp = ds.read_temp(roms[0])
    if current_temp >= start_temp + RISE_LIMIT:
        led.value(1)
    else:
        led.value(0)
    time.sleep(0.1)
explanation: The program records the DS18B20 temperature at startup as its reference. It then checks the temperature at least 750 milliseconds apart and turns on the built-in LED when the reading is 2 °C or more above that reference.

title: DS3231 clock
description: Set the DS3231 to 12:00:00, then blink the Pico’s built-in LED whenever the seconds change.
idea: The program sets the DS3231 real-time clock to 12:00:00, then the Pico's own LED blinks once each time the clock's seconds change
goal: Set the DS3231 to 12:00:00, then blink the Pico’s built-in LED whenever the seconds change.
behavior: When the program starts, it sets the DS3231 clock to 12:00:00.
The Pico’s built-in LED blinks once each time the clock’s seconds value changes.

parts.purpose: keep and report the time on the DS3231 clock module.

code:
from machine import Pin, I2C
from ds3231 import DS3231
import time

# Set how long the LED stays lit for each blink.
BLINK_TIME = 0.1

# Set up the clock on I2C0 and the Pico's built-in LED.
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(16), scl=Pin(17), freq=400000)
clock = DS3231(i2c)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Set the clock to noon on the current date.
clock.set_time(2026, 11, 26, 12, 0, 0)
previous_second = clock.time()[5]

# Blink once whenever the clock's seconds value changes.
while True:
    current_second = clock.time()[5]
    if current_second != previous_second:
        led.on()
        time.sleep(BLINK_TIME)
        led.off()
        previous_second = current_second
    time.sleep(0.05)
explanation: The program sets the DS3231 to 12:00:00 on November 26, 2026, then checks its seconds value. The Pico's built-in LED blinks briefly whenever that value changes.

title: Flame sensor
description: Use the Pico’s built-in LED to show when the flame sensor detects a flame.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on while the flame sensor sees a flame
goal: Use the Pico’s built-in LED to show when the flame sensor detects a flame.
behavior: The Pico’s LED turns on while the sensor sees a flame.
The LED turns off when the sensor no longer sees a flame.

parts.purpose: detect a small flame nearby; this is not a fire alarm.

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set how often the sensor is checked.
CHECK_DELAY = 0.05

# Set up the flame sensor input and the Pico's built-in LED.
flame_sensor = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Turn the LED on when the sensor detects a flame.
while True:
    if flame_sensor.value() == 0:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(CHECK_DELAY)
explanation: The program checks the flame sensor repeatedly. Its output is 0 when it detects a flame, so the built-in LED turns on then and turns off otherwise.

title: Hall sensor
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when a magnet is near the Hall sensor.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on while a magnet is near the Hall sensor
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when a magnet is near the Hall sensor.
behavior: When the Hall sensor detects a nearby magnet, the Pico’s built-in LED turns on.
When the magnet moves away, the LED turns off.

parts.purpose: detect a nearby magnet and control the LED automatically (use its D0 output)

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set how often the sensor is checked.
CHECK_DELAY = 0.05

# Set up the Hall sensor and the Pico's built-in LED.
hall_sensor = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Remember the sensor's reading when no magnet is nearby.
idle = hall_sensor.value()

# Turn the LED on when the sensor reading differs from its idle reading.
while True:
    if hall_sensor.value() != idle:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(CHECK_DELAY)
explanation: The program records the Hall sensor's reading at startup with no magnet nearby. It turns the built-in LED on when the sensor reading changes, and turns it off when the reading returns to its idle value.

title: IR obstacle sensor
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the IR obstacle sensor detects something in front of it.
idea: the Pico's own LED turns on while something is in front of the IR obstacle sensor
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the IR obstacle sensor detects something in front of it.
behavior: When something is in front of the sensor, the built-in LED turns on.
When nothing is detected, the built-in LED turns off.

parts.purpose: detect something in front of the Pico

code:

sensor = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

explanation: The program checks the IR sensor repeatedly. It turns the built-in LED on when the sensor detects an obstacle, and off when the way is clear.

title: Line sensor
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the line sensor detects a black line.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on while the line tracking sensor is over a black line
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the line sensor detects a black line.
behavior: The Pico’s built-in LED turns on over a black line.
The LED turns off over a light surface.

parts.purpose: detect the black line beneath the sensor, held close to the surface (about 1–15 mm)

code:

import time

CHECK_DELAY = 0.05

title: MPU-6050
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the MPU-6050 tilts more than 30 degrees from flat.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the MPU-6050 leans more than 30 degrees from flat
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the MPU-6050 tilts more than 30 degrees from flat.
behavior: The Pico checks the MPU-6050’s tilt.
The built-in LED turns on when the tilt is more than 30 degrees from flat.
The LED turns off when the tilt returns to 30 degrees or less.

parts.purpose: measure tilt from flat using the accelerometer.

code:
from machine import Pin, I2C
from mpu6050 import MPU6050
import time
import math

# Set the tilt limit in degrees
TILT_LIMIT = 30

# Set up the motion sensor and built-in LED
i2c = I2C(0, sda=Pin(16), scl=Pin(17), freq=400000)
mpu = MPU6050(i2c)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Check the tilt and update the LED
while True:
    x, y, z = mpu.acceleration()
    tilt = math.degrees(math.atan2(math.sqrt(x * x + y * y), abs(z)))
    led.value(1 if tilt > TILT_LIMIT else 0)
    time.sleep(0.1)
explanation: The program reads the MPU-6050 acceleration and calculates how far it is tilted from flat. The built-in LED turns on above 30 degrees and turns off at 30 degrees or less.

title: NTC thermistor
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the NTC thermistor gets at least 2 °C warmer than it was at startup.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the NTC thermistor's temperature is 2 °C higher than when the program started, for example when you hold it between your fingers.
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the NTC thermistor gets at least 2 °C warmer than it was at startup.
behavior: The program records the thermistor’s temperature when it starts.
The built-in LED turns on when the temperature is at least 2 °C above that starting temperature.
The LED turns off if the temperature drops below the threshold.

parts.purpose: measure temperature changes from the startup reading

code:
from machine import Pin, ADC
import math
import time

# Set the temperature change needed to turn on the LED.
TEMP_CHANGE = 2.0

# Set up the thermistor input and the Pico's built-in LED.
thermistor = ADC(26)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Take five readings to find the starting temperature.
total = 0.0
count = 0
for sample in range(5):
    value = thermistor.read_u16()
    if value != 0:
        resistance = 10000 * (65535 - value) / value
        temperature = 1 / (1 / 298.15 + math.log(resistance / 10000) / 3950) - 273.15
        total += temperature
        count += 1
    time.sleep(0.05)
start_temperature = total / count

# Keep checking the temperature and set the LED to match the threshold.
while True:
    total = 0.0
    count = 0
    for sample in range(5):
        value = thermistor.read_u16()
        if value != 0:
            resistance = 10000 * (65535 - value) / value
            temperature = 1 / (1 / 298.15 + math.log(resistance / 10000) / 3950) - 273.15
            total += temperature
            count += 1
        time.sleep(0.02)

    # Turn the LED on when warm enough, and off when it cools down.
    if count > 0 and total / count >= start_temperature + TEMP_CHANGE:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(0.1)
explanation: The program averages five thermistor readings at startup to record the starting temperature. It keeps averaging readings and turns the built-in LED on when the temperature is at least 2 °C warmer, turning it off again if the temperature falls below that threshold.

title: Photoresistor
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the photoresistor detects darkness.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the photoresistor gets dark, for example when you cover it with your hand
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when the photoresistor detects darkness.
behavior: The built-in LED turns on when the area around the photoresistor gets dark.
The built-in LED turns off when the area gets brighter.

parts.purpose: detect darkness and brighter light around it

code:
from machine import Pin, ADC
import time

# Set the light level below which the area is treated as dark.
DARK_THRESHOLD = 20000

# Set up the photoresistor input and the Pico's built-in LED.
light_sensor = ADC(26)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Turn on the LED in darkness and turn it off in brighter light.
while True:
    light_level = light_sensor.read_u16()
    led.value(1 if light_level < DARK_THRESHOLD else 0)
    time.sleep(0.1)
explanation: The program reads the photoresistor on GP26 and compares its reading with a threshold. The built-in LED turns on when the reading is below the threshold (darker) and turns off when it is above the threshold (brighter). Adjust DARK_THRESHOLD if needed for your room.

title: Reed switch
description: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when a magnet is near the reed switch.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on while a magnet is near the reed switch
goal: Turn on the Pico’s built-in LED when a magnet is near the reed switch.
behavior: When a magnet is near the reed switch, the built-in LED turns on.
When the magnet moves away, the LED turns off.

parts.purpose: detect when a magnet is nearby.

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set how long to wait before confirming a switch change.
DEBOUNCE_DELAY = 0.02

# Set up the reed switch and the Pico's built-in LED.
reed = Pin(16, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)
last_state = reed.value()
led.value(1 if last_state == 0 else 0)

# Check the switch and update the LED.
while True:
    current_state = reed.value()
    if current_state != last_state:
        time.sleep(DEBOUNCE_DELAY)
        current_state = reed.value()
        if current_state != last_state:
            last_state = current_state
    led.value(1 if last_state == 0 else 0)
    time.sleep(0.01)
explanation: The program checks the reed switch repeatedly and waits 20 ms to confirm a change. It turns the built-in LED on when the switch closes near a magnet, and off when the magnet moves away.

title: Soil moisture sensor
description: Turn on the Pico’s onboard LED when the soil sensor detects much wetter soil than it did at startup.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on when the capacitive soil moisture sensor reads much wetter than when the program started, for example when you put it in damp soil.
goal: Turn on the Pico’s onboard LED when the soil sensor detects much wetter soil than it did at startup.
behavior: At startup, the program records the soil sensor reading as the baseline.
The sensor reading goes down as the soil gets wetter.
The onboard LED turns on when the reading drops enough below the baseline, and turns off otherwise.

parts.purpose: measure how wet the soil is in the plant pot.

code:
from machine import Pin, ADC
import time

# Set how much lower the reading must be to count as much wetter.
WET_DROP = 5000

# Set up the soil sensor and the Pico's built-in LED.
soil = ADC(26)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Record the starting soil reading as the baseline.
baseline = soil.read_u16()

# Keep checking the soil and control the LED.
while True:
    reading = soil.read_u16()
    if reading <= baseline - WET_DROP:
        led.on()
    else:
        led.off()
    time.sleep(0.2)
explanation: The program records the soil sensor reading at startup, then checks it repeatedly. Because wetter soil gives a lower reading, the built-in LED turns on when the reading is at least 5000 counts below the startup baseline; otherwise, it stays off. Adjust WET_DROP to change how much wetter the soil must get.

title: Sound sensor
description: Toggle the Pico’s built-in LED with each clap detected by the sound sensor.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on or off with each clap the sound sensor hears
goal: Toggle the Pico’s built-in LED with each clap detected by the sound sensor.
behavior: The built-in LED starts off.
When the sound sensor detects a clap, the LED switches on or off.
The project waits briefly before detecting another clap, to help prevent one clap from toggling the LED twice.

parts.purpose: detect claps and other loud sounds above its set level

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set up the sound sensor and built-in LED.
sound_sensor = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)
led.value(0)

# Record when the sound sensor detects a clap.
clap_detected = False

def detect_clap(pin):
    global clap_detected
    clap_detected = True

# Watch for the sensor's brief low signal when a clap happens.
sound_sensor.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_FALLING, handler=detect_clap)

# Toggle the LED once per clap, then wait briefly to avoid repeats.
while True:
    if clap_detected:
        clap_detected = False
        led.toggle()
        time.sleep_ms(200)
        clap_detected = False
    time.sleep_ms(1)
explanation: The program starts with the built-in LED off and watches GP16 for a clap. Each detected clap toggles the LED, followed by a 200 ms pause to help prevent one clap from being counted twice.

title: Tilt switch
description: Turn on the Pico's built-in LED when the ball tilt switch is tilted.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on while the ball tilt switch is tilted
goal: Turn on the Pico's built-in LED when the ball tilt switch is tilted.
behavior: When the switch is tilted, the built-in LED turns on.
When the switch is upright, the built-in LED turns off.

parts.purpose: detect when the project is tilted or upright.

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set up the tilt switch and the built-in LED.
tilt = Pin(16, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)

# Check that the switch reading stays steady for about 50 ms.

    reading = tilt.value()

title: Touch sensor
description: Toggle the Pico’s built-in LED each time you touch the sensor.
idea: The Pico's own LED turns on or off each time you touch the touch sensor
goal: Toggle the Pico’s built-in LED each time you touch the sensor.
behavior: The built-in LED starts off.
Each new touch switches the LED to the opposite state.
The LED stays in that state until the next touch.

parts.purpose: toggle the built-in LED when touched once per touch event; release before touching again to toggle it again.

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set how long to wait after each check.
CHECK_DELAY = 0.02

# Set up the touch sensor and start the built-in LED off.
touch = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)
led.value(0)

# Let the sensor measure the untouched pad, then record its state.
time.sleep(0.5)
previous_touch = touch.value()

# Toggle the LED once when a new touch begins.
while True:
    current_touch = touch.value()
    if current_touch == 1 and previous_touch == 0:
        led.toggle()
    previous_touch = current_touch
    time.sleep(CHECK_DELAY)
explanation: The program starts the built-in LED off and waits half a second for the touch sensor to settle with the pad untouched. It toggles the LED when it detects a new touch, then waits for the pad to be released before detecting another touch.

title: Vibration motor
description: Run the vibration motor for half a second every 3 seconds.
idea: The vibration motor module vibrates for half a second every 3 seconds
goal: Run the vibration motor for half a second every 3 seconds.
behavior: The motor stays off for 2.5 seconds.
The motor vibrates for half a second.
This cycle repeats.

parts.purpose: vibrate on a repeating timer

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set the motor timing in seconds.
ON_TIME = 0.5
OFF_TIME = 2.5

# Set up the motor and make sure it starts off.
motor = Pin(16, Pin.OUT, value=0)

# Repeat the vibration cycle and stop the motor if the loop exits.
try:
    while True:
        motor.value(1)
        time.sleep(ON_TIME)
        motor.value(0)
        time.sleep(OFF_TIME)
finally:
    motor.value(0)

title: Vibration sensor
description: Blink the Pico’s built-in LED three times when a knock is detected.
idea: The Pico's own LED blinks 3 times when the vibration sensor feels a knock
goal: Blink the Pico’s built-in LED three times when a knock is detected.
behavior: When the vibration sensor detects a knock, the Pico’s built-in LED blinks three times.

parts.purpose: detect knocks or shaking near the Pico

code:
from machine import Pin
import time

# Set how long each blink lasts and how long to ignore repeat knocks.
BLINK_DELAY = 0.15
IGNORE_TIME = 200

# Read the sensor's idle value, and set up the built-in LED.
vibration = Pin(16, Pin.IN)
idle = vibration.value()
led = Pin("LED", Pin.OUT)
led.value(0)

# Watch for a sensor value that differs from its idle value.
while True:
    if vibration.value() != idle:
        # Blink the built-in LED three times for the knock.
        for _ in range(3):
            led.value(1)
            time.sleep(BLINK_DELAY)
            led.value(0)
            time.sleep(BLINK_DELAY)

        # Ignore brief repeats, then wait for the sensor to return to idle.
        time.sleep_ms(IGNORE_TIME)
        while vibration.value() != idle:
            time.sleep_ms(1)

    # Check the sensor often so short signals are less likely to be missed.
    time.sleep_ms(1)
explanation: The program records the vibration sensor’s value while it is still, then watches for a different value. When it detects a knock, the built-in LED blinks three times and the program briefly ignores the sensor before watching again.

title: Sound board

Each sensor gives its own signal. A magnet on the reed switch plays a high tone on the passive buzzer, and a clap plays a low tone. A black line under the line sensor plays a short melody. A knock on the vibration sensor makes the active buzzer beep twice.

code:
from machine import Pin, PWM
import time

# Set up the passive buzzer quiet and prepare the input sensors.
Pin(16, Pin.OUT, value=1)
reed = Pin(20, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)
sound = Pin(22, Pin.IN)
line = Pin(17, Pin.IN)
vibration = Pin(21, Pin.IN)
buzzer = Pin(18, Pin.OUT, value=1)

# Remember sensor states and prepare flags for quick sensor interrupts.
reed_old = reed.value()
line_old = line.value()
vibration_idle = vibration.value()
sound_hit = False
vibration_hit = False

def sound_irq(pin):
    global sound_hit
    sound_hit = True

def vibration_irq(pin):
    global vibration_hit
    vibration_hit = True

# Watch for brief sound and vibration signals between loop checks.
sound.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_FALLING, handler=sound_irq)
vibration.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING | Pin.IRQ_FALLING, handler=vibration_irq)

# Play one passive-buzzer note, then put its pin back in the quiet state.
def play_note(frequency, duration):
    pwm = PWM(Pin(16))
    pwm.freq(frequency)
    pwm.duty_u16(32768)
    time.sleep_ms(duration)
    pwm.deinit()
    Pin(16, Pin.OUT, value=1)

# Check sensors often and play the sound for each new trigger.
while True:
    reed_now = reed.value()
    line_now = line.value()
    if reed_now != reed_old:
        time.sleep_ms(20)
        reed_now = reed.value()
        if reed_now == 0:
            play_note(1000, 250)
        reed_old = reed_now
    if sound_hit:
        sound_hit = False
        play_note(262, 300)
        time.sleep_ms(200)
    if line_now != line_old:
        if line_now == 1:
            play_note(1047, 150)
            play_note(784, 150)
            play_note(880, 150)
        line_old = line_now
    if vibration_hit:
        vibration_hit = False
        if vibration.value() != vibration_idle:
            buzzer.value(0)
            time.sleep_ms(120)
            buzzer.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(120)
            buzzer.value(0)
            time.sleep_ms(120)
            buzzer.value(1)
            time.sleep_ms(200)
    time.sleep_ms(1)
explanation: The program watches the four sensors and plays the matching sound when each one is triggered. The line sensor plays a short, higher-pitched melody through the passive buzzer, and a vibration triggers two beeps from the active buzzer.
